statement.summary: Theorem 4.7 is frozen in Paper/S13_AbelianGroups.lean (group 13) as `abelianEnumStatement`: for a finite abelian group G (a type with `[AddCommGroup G] [Finite G]`) and σ ≥ 1, |S_G| cast to ℤ equals `abelianRHS (Nat.card G) (pRank G) σ`, the paper's sum re-indexed by the divisors h ≠ 1 of R = ∏_{p∣N} p^{d_p} (`rankRad`), as the core's `enumerationRHS` is for Theorem 4.4. Unlike Theorem 4.4 (bridge `P04.rankVectorReindexStatement`), no frozen Prop transcribes the vector-indexed sum for general G: the re-indexing v ↦ h = ∏ p^{v_p} has to be checked by reading `abelianRHS` and `coeffA`. The setting paragraph is covered by `pRank` + `pRankPowStatement` (the p-rank), `pTorsionVectorSpaceStatement` (G[p] is an F_p-vector space of dimension d_p), `rectCardStatement` and `rectRankStatement` (rectangular tori; the instance of the theorem is `rectEnumStatement`). The last sentence ('this is Theorem 4.4') is `squareStatement` (right sides agree) with `bridgeStatement` (the shift-symmetry predicates agree). Proofs: Paper/Proofs/P13_AbelianGroups*.lean, checked by AuditPaper (group 13).

lean_decls.role: statement (last sentence: right sides on ℤ_n^d)
statement (setting: G[p] is an F_p-vector space of dimension d_p)

deltas: Alphabet Σ = `Fin σ`; a finite abelian group is a type with `[AddCommGroup G] [Finite G]` (any universe), N = `Nat.card G`; |S_G| = `Nat.card` of the subtype of `IsShiftSymmetricG` configurations G → Fin σ, cast to ℤ (the right side has signs).

Shift-symmetric: `IsShiftSymmetricG s` := ∃ v ≠ 0, ∀ u, s (u + v) = s u (the paper's (τ_v s)(u) = s(u+v), i.e. Stab(s) ≠ {0}); stabilizers are not formalized separately. On ℤ_n^d it is the core's `IsShiftSymmetric` (`bridgeStatement`).

p-rank: `pRank G p` is the exponent of p in |G[p]|; `pRankPowStatement` certifies |G[p]| = p^{pRank G p} for prime p, and `pTorsionVectorSpaceStatement` (group-13 supplement, 2026-11-08) certifies that G[p] is an F_p-vector space (ZMod p acting naturally) of dimension pRank G p.

The vector-indexed sum is re-indexed by the divisors h ≠ 1 of R = ∏_{p∣N} p^{d_p} (`rankRad`): v_p = v_p(h), |v| = Ω(h) (`bigOmega`), product over the primes of h only (r_{d_p}(p,0) = 1), as in the core's `enumerationRHS`. No frozen bridge to the vector-indexed form exists for general G (Theorem 4.4 has `P04.rankVectorReindexStatement`); on ℤ_n^d, `squareStatement` reduces it to `enumerationRHS`.

Exponents are ℕ-quotients N / h. Exact because h ∣ R ∣ N (p^{d_p} = |G[p]| divides N by Lagrange; helper `pRank_pow_dvd` in the proofs); unlike Theorem 4.4 (`exponentEncodingStatement`) no frozen Prop records the exactness.
Rectangular tori are `∀ i : Fin d, ZMod (n i)` with all n i ≥ 1 (ZMod 0 = ℤ); the paper's number of factors m is `d` here.

'this is Theorem 4.4' = the right sides agree (`squareStatement`, for n ≥ 1 and every d, σ) and the predicates agree (`bridgeStatement`, for every n, d, σ): both are stated more generally than Theorem 4.4's n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 1.

Not frozen: the opening sentence (a remark on the structure of a proof; its torsion fact is Lemma 3.3, `P02.torsionLemmaStatement`) and the proof. 'An F_p-vector space', listed as not frozen in the S13 docstring, is frozen in the group-13 supplement (`pTorsionVectorSpaceStatement`, Run 046).

maps.label: |S_G| = Σ_{v ≠ 0, 0 ≤ v_p ≤ d_p} (−1)^{1+|v|} ∏ r_{d_p}(p,v_p) σ^{N/∏ p^{v_p}}

lean.text:
(Nat.card {s : G → Fin σ // IsShiftSymmetricG s} : ℤ)
      = abelianRHS (Nat.card G) (pRank G) σ

maps.note: Equation in ℤ. The right side is the DIVISOR-indexed `abelianRHS` (see the maps rhs, idx, v0, sign, prod, exp); no frozen Prop states the vector-indexed form for general G.

maps.label: every finite abelian group G (written additively)

tex.text:
For a finite abelian group $G$ of order $N$,
written additively,

maps.note: A finite abelian group, written additively, is a type with `AddCommGroup` and `Finite` instances. 'For every' G and σ: the Prop takes them as parameters and its `_proved` theorem quantifies over them.

maps.label: N = order of G
maps.note: N is `Nat.card G`, passed to `abelianRHS` as its first argument.

maps.label: σ ≥ 1
maps.note: Verbatim antecedent; σ = 1 allowed, as for counting statements.

maps.label: alphabet Σ with |Σ| = σ ↦ Fin σ

tex.text:
a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ with
$\sigma=|\Sigma|\ge2$ (for counting statements, $\sigma=1$ is also allowed)

maps.note: Only |Σ| enters; configurations are functions G → Fin σ.

maps.label: |S_G|: configurations G → Σ fixed by some nonzero translation

tex.text:
Configurations
$G\to\Sigma$, translations, stabilizers, and $S_G$ are defined as in
Section~\ref{sec:model} with $\A$ replaced by $G$

lean.text: Nat.card {s : G → Fin σ // IsShiftSymmetricG s}
∃ v : G, v ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ u : G, s (u + v) = s u

maps.note: S_G = {s : Stab(s) ≠ {0}} with 𝒜 replaced by G: some v ≠ 0 has (τ_v s)(u) = s(u+v) = s(u) for all u. Stabilizers are not a Lean object here; only this predicate is used. |·| = `Nat.card` of the subtype.

maps.label: the right side ↦ abelianRHS N d_• σ

lean.text: ∑ h ∈ (rankRad N dp).divisors.erase 1, coeffA dp h * (σ : ℤ) ^ (N / h)

maps.note: Bijection v ↦ h = ∏_{p∣N} p^{v_p} between the paper's index set and the divisors h ≠ 1 of R = ∏_{p∣N} p^{d_p}, with v_p = v_p(h); term by term: sign, coefficient product, exponent (maps below). The bijection itself is not a frozen Prop; check it by reading.

maps.label: v = (v_p)_{p∣N}, 0 ≤ v_p ≤ d_p ↔ h ∣ R = ∏_{p∣N} p^{d_p}
maps.note: h ∣ R iff h has only prime factors p ∣ N and v_p(h) ≤ d_p for each; so h ↔ v is a bijection (also for N = 1: R = 1 and both index sets are empty after removing 0). d_p is `dp p` = `pRank G p`.

maps.label: v ≠ 0 ↔ h ≠ 1
maps.note: v = 0 corresponds to h = ∏ p^0 = 1, which is erased.

maps.label: (−1)^{1+|v|} ↔ (−1)^{1+Ω(h)}
maps.note: |v| is defined in Theorem 4.4 (Σ_i v_i), here Σ_p v_p = Ω(h), the number of prime factors of h with multiplicity. Sign in ℤ.

maps.label: ∏_{p∣N} r_{d_p}(p,v_p) ↔ ∏_{p∣h} r_{d_p}(p, v_p(h))

lean.text: ∏ p ∈ h.primeFactors, (rdCoeff p (h.factorization p) (dp p) : ℤ)

maps.note: The Lean product runs over the primes of h only; the primes p ∣ N with v_p = 0 contribute r_{d_p}(p,0) = 1 (`gaussBinom q dd 0 = 1`, `0.choose 2 = 0`), so nothing is lost. v_p = `h.factorization p`. Cast ℕ → ℤ.

maps.label: r_{d_p}(p,v) = p^{C(v,2)} [d_p v]_p

lean.text: | dd + 1, r + 1 => gaussBinom q dd r + q ^ (r + 1) * gaussBinom q dd (r + 1)

maps.note: Definition 4.3's r_d with d replaced by d_p: the third argument of `rdCoeff p v dd` is `dp p`. Gaussian binomial by q-Pascal; agreement with the paper's product formula is the P01 fidelity Prop.

maps.label: σ^{N/∏_p p^{v_p}} ↔ σ^{N / h}
maps.note: Power in ℤ with a natural-number exponent.

maps.label: N/∏_p p^{v_p} as ℕ-division N / h (exact)
maps.note: h = ∏ p^{v_p}. ℕ-division, exact because h ∣ R ∣ N (each p^{d_p} = |G[p]| divides N). The exactness is not a frozen Prop here (Theorem 4.4 has `P04.exponentEncodingStatement`); it is a fact to check by reading (proved as the helper `pRank_pow_dvd`).

maps.label: opening sentence: ℤ_n^d enters the proof only through its order and p-torsion

tex.text:
enters the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-enum} only through its order
and its $p$-torsion, which is $\FF_p^d$ for every prime $p\mid n$

maps.note: A remark on the structure of the proof of Theorem 4.4, not frozen (S13 docstring). Its mathematical fact, the p-torsion of ℤ_n^d is F_p^d, is Lemma 3.3 (`P02.torsionLemmaStatement`, group 02).

maps.label: G[p] = {g ∈ G : pg = 0}
maps.note: pg is the ℕ-scalar multiple `p • g`; G[p] is the subtype in `pRank`/`pRankPowStatement` and the subgroup `pTorsion` (same carrier) in `pTorsionVectorSpaceStatement`.

maps.label: G[p] is an F_p-vector space

lean.text:
∃ _ : Module (ZMod p) (pTorsion G p),
      (∀ (c : ZMod p) (g : pTorsion G p), ((c • g : pTorsion G p) : G) = c.val • (g : G))

maps.note: Frozen in the group-13 supplement (2026-11-08): for prime p, G[p] carries a ZMod p-module structure (ZMod p = F_p) whose action is the natural one, c • g = c.val • g. The structure is asserted to exist; the action clause makes it the paper's.

maps.label: d_p = dim_{F_p} G[p] ↔ exponent of p in |G[p]|

lean.text: Module.finrank (ZMod p) (pTorsion G p) = pRank G p

maps.note: The formal p-rank `pRank G p` is v_p(|G[p]|); `pTorsionVectorSpaceStatement` certifies that for prime p it equals dim_{F_p} G[p] (`Module.finrank (ZMod p)` of the structure above), so the paper's definition of d_p and the one Theorem 4.7 uses agree. For non-prime p the Lean value is 0 and the paper does not use it.

maps.label: rectangular torus ℤ_{n_1} × ⋯ × ℤ_{n_m}
maps.note: The product is the Π-type `∀ i : Fin d, ZMod (n i)`; the number of factors m is called `d` here (it is not the dimension of the theorem).

maps.label: n_i ≥ 1 (implicit in ℤ_{n_i})
maps.note: `ZMod 0 = ℤ` is infinite, so n_i = 0 is excluded; n_i = 1 (a trivial factor) is allowed.

maps.label: N = ∏_i n_i

lean.text: Nat.card (∀ i, ZMod (n i)) = ∏ i, n i

maps.note: Equality in ℕ.

maps.label: d_p = |{i : p ∣ n_i}|

lean.text: p.Prime → pRank (∀ i, ZMod (n i)) p = rectRank n p

maps.note: For every prime p (the p-rank is defined for primes).

maps.label: Theorem 4.7 instantiated on rectangular tori

lean.text:
(Nat.card {s : (∀ i, ZMod (n i)) → Fin σ // IsShiftSymmetricG s} : ℤ)
      = abelianRHS (∏ i, n i) (rectRank n) σ

maps.note: Not a separate sentence of the paper: the theorem with N and d_p replaced by the setting's formulas for rectangular tori (rect.N, rect.dp). Frozen so that this instance is certified directly; the example of Corollary B.1(i) (Corollary 4.8(i) in v10) is proved from it.

maps.label: for G = ℤ_n^d (d_p = d for p ∣ n) this is Theorem 4.4

tex.text:
$G=\ZZ_n^d$, where $d_p=d$ for every $p\mid n$, this is
Theorem~\ref{thm:main-enum}

lean.text: abelianRHS (n ^ d) (rectRank (fun _ : Fin d => n)) σ = enumerationRHS n d σ
∀ s : Config n d (Fin σ), IsShiftSymmetricG s ↔ IsShiftSymmetric s

maps.note: Two Props: on ℤ_n^d the right side of Theorem 4.7 is Theorem 4.4's (divisor-indexed) `enumerationRHS` (`squareStatement`), and the shift-symmetry predicate is the core's (`bridgeStatement`), so both sides of Theorem 4.4 (`enumerationStatement`) are recovered.

maps.label: G = ℤ_n^d ↦ Lat n d, N = n^d

lean.text: ∀ s : Config n d (Fin σ), IsShiftSymmetricG s ↔ IsShiftSymmetric s
∃ v : Lat n d, v ≠ 0 ∧ shift v s = s

maps.note: ℤ_n^d is `Lat n d = Fin d → ZMod n` (`Config n d (Fin σ)` = its configurations); on it `IsShiftSymmetricG` is the core's `IsShiftSymmetric`, so |S_G| is Theorem 4.4's left side. N = n^d (rectCardStatement with n_i = n).

maps.label: d_p = d for every p ∣ n
maps.note: The ranks of ℤ_n^d enter as `rectRank` of the constant family: d if p ∣ n, 0 otherwise (such p do not divide N = n^d and do not occur). That these are the p-ranks of `Lat n d` is `rectRankStatement` with n_i = n.

maps.label: Theorem 4.4 (its right side)

lean.text:
(Nat.card {s : Config n dd (Fin σ) // IsShiftSymmetric s} : ℤ)
      = enumerationRHS n dd σ

maps.note: Theorem 4.4 is the frozen `enumerationStatement` (divisor form); its link to the paper's rank-vector form is `P04.rankVectorReindexStatement` (see the item of Theorem 4.4).

maps.label: hypotheses of the last sentence: n ≥ 1, any d and σ
maps.note: Theorem 4.4 assumes n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 1; `squareStatement` holds for n ≥ 1 and all d, σ, and `bridgeStatement` for all n, d, σ. Harmless strengthening.
